question: Does a falling-pressure storm cue explain strong chorus activation beyond antecedent rainfall amount and rainfall recency?
sample: Same midpoint-qualified NAAMP matched pairs used by the hydric-cue analysis.

weather_source.spatial_link: nearest ERA5 0.25 degree grid cell to route centroid

cues.pressure_drop_6h: MSL pressure at t-6h minus MSL pressure at t, in hPa; positive means falling pressure into the survey.
cues.pressure_drop_24h: MSL pressure at t-24h minus MSL pressure at t; secondary.
cues.pressure_fall_advantage: wet-run pressure drop minus dry-run pressure drop; positive means the wetter survey experienced a stronger pressure fall.

primary_model: strong_new_score ~ rain_contrast + rain72_amount_difference_z + pressure6_advantage_z + temp_difference + doy_difference + year_gap + C(State) + C(RunNumber), route-clustered covariance.

primary_predictions.accumulated_rain_independent: rain72_amount_difference_z beta >0 with complete 95% CI >0 after pressure adjustment.
primary_predictions.accumulated_over_barometric: rain72 supported while pressure6 is not supported.

secondary: Replace 6h pressure drop with 24h pressure drop.
Repeat primary in same-observer + physically stable pairs.
minimum_gate: At least 3500 pairs and 500 routes; MSL pressure variable identity, units and finite-range audit must pass.
interpretation: Pressure tendency is an atmospheric storm cue, not a direct hydrological state.
Non-support does not rule out pressure cues at other temporal scales.
No causal mediation or RC11 manuscript change is authorized.
